summary: Abe proves both positivity and Qℓ-realizability of the higher-dimensional local Artin character for regular local rings containing a finite field. The proof combines an equivariant local-Fourier total-dimension identity with a relative Lefschetz–Verdier trace and ULA extension after alteration. Ordinary nearby cycles and cohomological correspondences are existing atlas imports. General-coherent-base extension, categorical relative traces, projective Swan modules and the geometric Artin theorem require continuations. This is a substantive partial extraction: the whole main paper is read, but the external Kato–Saito–Saito reduction and recursive general-base proof leaves remain open.

conventions.C1: A is a regular local ring with maximal ideal m and finite group G acting by local automorphisms. A^G is Noetherian, A is finite over A^G, A/Iσ has finite length for every σ≠1, Iσ=(a−σ(a):a∈A), and A^G/(m∩A^G)→A/m is an isomorphism. The main theorem additionally assumes A contains a finite field, hence characteristic p>0; ℓ is invertible in A.
conventions.C2: In the geometric theorem k is algebraically closed of characteristic p>0, ℓ≠p, S is the strict henselization of P¹_t at 0, S′ that of P¹_t′ at ∞′, and η′ its generic point. f:X→S is flat of finite type, X regular, G finite acting by S-automorphisms, the union of the fixed loci for nonidentity elements has underlying set {x}, and f is smooth outside the closed point x. Λ=Qℓ(ζp), with a fixed nontrivial ψ:Fp→Λ×. Nearby-cycle complexes and traces are unshifted cohomological objects; traces mean alternating traces.
conventions.C3: For ramification modules K=Frac(k{t}) with k separably closed of characteristic p>0, Γ=Gal(Ksep/K), ℓ≠p, G finite commuting with Γ. A chosen Galois tower and compatible isomorphisms of Swan modules are data at integral level. They are not declared canonical. Rational coefficients L are finite extensions of Qℓ.
conventions.C4: Dctf means constructible complexes of finite Tor dimension. For the cited Lu–Zheng dualizability theorem use a Noetherian commutative torsion coefficient ring killed by an integer invertible on the Noetherian base. Actual Theorem 1.5 and finite-level trace application use finite rings; no unchecked extension to arbitrary non-Noetherian coefficients is claimed.
conventions.C5: RL(G) is K0 of perfect L[G]-complexes. In characteristic zero it is compared to the existing split representation ring via semisimplicity and Euler characteristic, not identified by notation alone. DΛ-perf(Λ[G]) means perfect over Λ, not necessarily over Λ[G].
conventions.C6: All library citations are exact existing carriers/theorems only. Added planning API and tests are specifications for reuse/adapters, not claims that wrappers or the paper are formalized. Items depend on the conventions and the explicitly named gap gates as well as their item dependencies.

items.name: Geometric Serre conjecture: positivity
items.statement: Under C1 with A containing a finite field and ℓ invertible in A, aG is the character of an actual finite-dimensional Qbarℓ-representation of G.

items.name: Geometric Serre conjecture: Qℓ realization
items.statement: Under the same hypotheses as G06, the Artin representation is realizable over Qℓ for every ℓ invertible in A. This is stronger than a Qℓ-valued virtual trace identity.

items.name: Regular-character ambiguity in a nonidentity trace identity
items.statement: For a finite group G over a characteristic-zero field, adding a multiple of the regular character changes only the value at 1. Therefore the nonidentity trace formula alone does not fix the normalized identity value, positivity or rational descent.

items.name: Tame curve tower different formula
items.statement: For a tower of finite separable smooth curve germs X→qY→gS over an algebraically closed field, d(f)=d(q)+e(q)d(g), where d is the local different exponent and e the ramification index. For the quotient by G at a unique totally ramified point e(q)=|G| and d(q)=aG(1). Thus μf−aG(1)=e(q)d(g), not in general d(g).

items.name: Identity-element trace under an étale quotient parameter

routes.title: Grothendieck groups, Cartan maps, and Euler forms, Part II: equivariant perfect traces
routes.reason: The upstream roadmap supplies K0 and bounded comparisons but expressly excludes perfect-category machinery. The new interfaces are group-ring-perfect versus coefficient-perfect categories, equivariant strictification/trace additivity and the tensor comparison, not new K0 carriers.
routes.brief: Build on Grothendieck groups, Cartan maps, and Euler forms (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GrothendieckEulerForms), importing Layer 2's K0 and bounded comparisons and the pinned Euler–Poincaré declarations. Import bounded projective coefficient models from General algebraic K-theory (GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.4:construction) and derived tensor/enhancement from Enhanced derived categories of sheaves (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1). Construct the relevant perfect subcategories and prove their comparison with these models, without constructing another K-theory spectrum. For finite G over a characteristic-zero field L, compare K0(Dperf(L[G])) with the existing split representation ring and its injective character map. For a commutative Noetherian ring Λ, define DΛ-perf(Λ[G]) by underlying Λ-perfectness. Construct the action of each σ through left multiplication on the right regular group algebra, strictify derived maps to bounded Λ-projective equivariant complexes, and prove trace additivity by the mapping cone. State the distinction from arbitrary triangulated endomorphisms identified by Ferrand. Prove the K0 tensor pairing when the right factor is perfect over Λ[Δ], with a coefficient-perfect Δ×G module on the left-action side. Test shifts, cones, a group whose order is not invertible in Λ, and failure of the inference from Λ-perfect to Λ[G]-perfect. This early algebraic supplier must not depend on Abe's ramification theorem or the relative geometric trace.

routes.title: Étale duality, cycle classes and perverse sheaves, Part II: relative categorical traces
routes.reason: EDC.8 plans ordinary cohomological correspondences, but not the Lu–Zheng symmetric-monoidal 2-category, ULA-dualizability criterion and arbitrary base-change relative trace needed to deform between parameter fibers. This is distinct from the pending microlocal/polar-bounds Part II.
routes.brief: Import ordinary six operations, duality and cohomological correspondences from Étale duality, cycle classes and perverse sheaves (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.0, EDC.1, EDC.8), and the shared derived tensor/enhancement from EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1. Construct Corr(S), with proper 2-morphisms, and the right-lax symmetric monoidal Grothendieck construction for g_!f*. Add only the missing generic 2-categorical trace/coherence interfaces, coordinating their reusable home with the existing categorical owners rather than duplicating their category carriers. Define dualizable objects, endomorphisms and ΩC, the trace functor and its symmetric monoidal naturality. Under the Noetherian coefficient/base hypotheses of Lu–Zheng Theorem 2.16, prove the LA/ULA-dualizability criterion and identify the dual with relative Verdier duality. Construct the fixed-locus trace and prove Proposition 2.26 base-change compatibility. Import general-base ULA extension from the nearby-cycles continuation, not as an axiom. For Abe's application use one chosen σ at a time, normalize the curve alteration to a connected finite cover, and identify the relative trace target with Λ by nil-invariance and connectedness. Compare with the scalar perfect trace from GrothendieckEulerFormsPartIIEquivariantTraces. Tests include a point, a disconnected parameter countertest and a nonreduced fixed scheme. Do not merge this work with EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheavesPartIIMicrolocal; that continuation owns characteristic-cycle/polar statements.

routes.title: Lefschetz pencils, nearby cycles and vanishing cycles, Part II: general bases and local Fourier transforms
routes.reason: LPV.0 explicitly restricts its base-change/construction results to the excellent finite-type trait setting. Abe Lemma 1.4/Theorem 1.5 use arbitrary coherent bases and alterations; local Fourier transforms and total-dimension identities also have no current LPV layer.
routes.brief: Import the actual trait RΨ/RΦ and strict-local Milnor-fiber API from Lefschetz pencils, nearby cycles and vanishing cycles (LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.0), constructible coefficients from EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.0 and enhancement from EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1. First prove continuity of Hom and bounded constructible derived categories over affine inverse limits of coherent schemes with Noetherian coefficients. Define goodness and strict-local cohomological properness from Orgogozo, transcribe the alteration/modification theorems with their full hypotheses, and construct the absolute-integral-closure extension Rj*Fξ with constructibility, finite Tor and ULA proofs. Descend the complex, open identification and chosen endomorphism to prove exactly Abe Theorem 1.5: finite coefficient ring, coherent base with finitely many irreducible components, finite-presentation f, ULA input on an open and a specified σ/α. Do not assume proper f or extend to a simultaneous coherent G-action without proof. Treat the finite-cover refinement as a separate Abe–Gabber input. Next construct the Artin–Schreier kernel and local Fourier functor, proving concentration, exactness, rank and Swan formulas from Laumon. Import only the early Swan-module prefix of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentationsPartIIGeometricArtin and the equivariant perfect-trace/tensor prefix of GrothendieckEulerFormsPartIIEquivariantTraces. Prove the group-ring-perfect regular Fourier class, derived tensor interchange, finite-to-adic comparisons and local total-dimension identity. Deduce support at the isolated point independently of the geometric trace theorem; then prove Proposition 2.5(2). The late Artin theorem consumes these outputs, so never impose a cyclic whole-roadmap prerequisite. Tests distinguish full-trait constant input from punctured-trait zero extension, degree-one Euler signs, regular versus augmentation input, and finite-level versus rational coefficients.

routes.title: Arithmetic Galois representations and conductors, Part II: geometric Artin representations
routes.reason: R01.3 supplies numerical arithmetic conductors; it does not assert Serre's representation theorem for arbitrary regular local rings or provide chosen projective Swan modules over henselian geometric traits with separably closed residue field.
routes.brief: Build on Arithmetic Galois representations and conductors (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1, R01.3) for continuous actions, stable lattices and numerical conductors. Import general ramification/valuation infrastructure from Local fields and ramification (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification) and finite-group character theory from tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/CharacterTheory, reusing the pinned split representation ring and character injectivity. The early prefix extends the conductor input to the henselian geometric trait K=Frac(k{t}), k separably closed of characteristic p, and constructs Serre's projective integral Swan modules, chosen quotient-compatible towers, exact torsion/integral Swan functors and lattice/tower-independent rational total-dimension classes. These are early suppliers to local Fourier theory, not consumers of the main theorem. The late prefix defines admissible regular-local actions and aG(σ)=−length(A/Iσ) for σ≠1 with aG(1) fixed by zero augmentation. Import relative trace and local Fourier results from the two geometric continuations; prove Theorem 1.6 for σ≠1 under its full regularity, flatness, isolated-fixed-point and smooth-off-x hypotheses. Read and decompose Kato–Saito–Saito Conjecture 5.1/Lemma 5.3 before deducing that when A contains a finite field, aG is an actual character and is realizable over every Qℓ with ℓ invertible in A. Do not deduce positivity or Qℓ descent from a virtual trace identity alone. Add the Katz/Laumon models and corrected curve identity d(f)=d(q)+e(q)d(g); test tame C2 with x² followed by u³ and the characteristic-two nonreduced fixed-locus example. Keep the W(k)[1/p]-rationality assertion as a conjecture, not a target claimed proved.

gaps.detail: Obtain and read Kato–Saito–Saito, Artin characters for algebraic surfaces, Conjecture 5.1 and Lemma 5.3 with the complete proof.
